item.title: Narwhal and Tusk: Moving the Bottleneck Out of BFT Consensus
item.description: For most of the last decade, work on fast Byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT) consensus has focused on one number: message complexity, meaning how many protocol messages the validators exchange per decision. HotStuff (Yin et al., 2019) brought that number down to linear in the partially synchronous setting by routing all votes through a leader. The paper by Danezis, Kokoris-Kogias, Sonnino and Spiegelman, published at EuroSys 2022, argues that this target misses where the cost actually sits in a real ledger. The expensive part is not agreeing on an order. It is moving the transactions themselves to every validator, reliably.

item.title: A BFT ordering service for Fabric, and the library under it
item.description: Fabric’s ordering service receives endorsed transactions from clients and emits a stream of blocks. When we wrote this paper the latest release, v2.3, ran it on Raft, which tolerates crashes and nothing worse. The paper describes how my co-authors and I made Fabric Byzantine fault-tolerant end to end: a consensus library in Go, based on the BFT-SMaRt protocol, and the changes to the orderer, the peer and the client that had to come with it.
